Row.txt_code:
A beautiful Inspirational Scroll, created by Anna Reyner.
 
Objective:
This workshop combines writing and Liquid Watercolors beautifully.  These fun watercolor materials can help us reach our feelings, and create an Inspirational Scroll.

Materials: (Workshop supplies can be purchased at www.discountschoolsupply.com )
Liquid Watercolors in primary or assorted colors
Metallic Liquid Watercolors in silver and gold (optional for added accents)
Spray bottles
Squeeze bottles to use with Metallic Watercolors
Mural Art Paper/ Paper Drop Cloth (any size - we made ours 12x20)
2 Dowels or chop sticks (2 inches wider than the Mural Art Paper used)
Permanent markers
Colored ribbon cord
Scissors
Tacky Glue
Card stock or natural fiber paper for words and stencils
Paper towels
Plastic stencils (Optional)
Bell or chimes (Optional)
Writing prompts (word prompt on strength, hope and courage)

  
  The poem can be decorated too! 
Variations for age levels:
This workshop works best with children who can write. With children who are unable to write, they can draw pictures or have leaders write what they would like to say. For a younger child you might want to prepare the scroll by adding the dowels in advance.

Timeframe:
Intro: 5 minutes
Warm Up: 10 minutes
Demo/Creation: 35 minutes to 1 hour
Closing: 10 minutes       Total Time: 1 to 1 1/2 hours


   
  An assortment of fun materials.
 
Set Up:
Prepare the supplies by placing the Watercolor paint in spray bottles and the Metallic Liquid Watercolors in squeeze bottles (the metallic colors will be drizzled or dripped as accent or highlight colors). Cut the Mural Art Paper in any size you like, ideally the Mural Art Paper should be at least 60% longer than wide to make a rectangular panel shape.

Spraying the Liquid Watercolors can be messy, so prep the tables with washable tablecloths or newspaper. You may even want to do the spraying outside where there is room to spread out and where the sun will highlight the colors!

Introduction:
Make sure to take time to welcome everyone, and let them know that their being there and participating is really appreciated. Have soothing music on as the children settle in. "This art time is a special 'window of time' for you, where we will be using words and watercolors to reach into our hearts for deep feelings of inspiration, reminding ourselves how strong we are, and creating beautiful Inspirational Scrolls.

"We’ll begin our workshop by spending time together and thinking about the people in our life who have helped us feel how strong we really are inside. We’ll begin our art project with a demonstration of how to spray the Liquid Watercolors to get beautiful colorful effects. Then we’ll paste the words we've written onto our art panels, and add rainbow silk cord and beads to make Inspirational Scrolls!"

Warm Up:
Pass around a bell, and have each participant take turns striking the bell as it is passed around the circle. As they strike the bell, have them say, “I'm thinking about ..." and name someone who has given them strength or shown them how strong they are. Pause between each person so they can think about who they will choose to talk about.

The leader can begin, setting an example by striking the bell and saying something like, “As I ring this bell, I'm thinking about my mother Angela whose love makes me strong.” Then the leader will pass the instrument for each participant to take a turn ringing the bell and saying his or her own words.

When everyone is finished, have the children hold hands while the leader says, “We're meeting here today to respect ourselves, to respect the process of healing that is alive in us, and to respect those in our lives who have shown us how strong we are. We are all stronger today because of your being here and participating. Thank you for being here."

 
 Spraying the Liquid Watercolors to layer colors.
  
 
  You can use stencils to create designs of all shapes!
  
 
  Shade and layer stencils to create beautiful effects.
Demo:
Show the children how to use the Liquid Watercolor sprays, using a practice panel of Mural Art Paper. Demonstrate how to use the "mist" spray option rather than the "stream" spray option on the spray bottles.

Demonstrate how by layering primary colors (red, yellow, blue) there are lots of possibilities.  By spraying first yellow then overlapping with red shows how the colors blend to make orange where they overlap. Then add a stencil, either a plastic pre-made stencil or hand-made stencil, and spray over that. Repeat this process by lifting, overlapping, and re-spraying with various colors.

A hand-made stencil can be made by tearing card stock paper into various shapes. One can then use the cut out itself or the paper it was cut from. One can also use leaves or other objects as stencils too, which is especially fun if the project is taking place outside. When using the stencils, spray from the side (not straight on) for a better effect and more options. For a "shading" effect spray one side with a darker color, then spray with another color from a different side to make it two toned.

When there are a lot of layers, the stencil image can disappear. If the participant wants to see the stencil pattern, encourage them not to layer too many colors on the scroll, and to make sure to use the stencil towards the end.

Keep in mind, this project is all about mixing color, so there are no "mess ups." Play with the paint until you like the colors and patterns that are created. Even the darker "muddy" areas can be highlighted by adding the metallic colors. Take gold and silver watercolors and drizzle or drip those as accent colors on top, or you can even paint them onto the scroll. When you are finished painting, lay the Mural Art Paper to dry on paper towels.

Creation:
Now, we will create Inspirational Scrolls or wall hangings that help us remember how strong we are inside, and remember our special time and space together today.

 
 You can even use a real leaf as a stencil!
  
 
  Add accents with Metallic Watercolors.
Step 1:
Spray entire panel with a variety of colors. Use stencils to create patterns, layer, and overlap colors.

Step 2:
Add gold and silver Metallic Watercolors by dripping, drizzling, or painting them on as accent or highlight colors.

Step 3:
Put the scroll aside to dry.

Step 4:
While the scroll panel dries we will do a writing exercise. Ask the group to think about the people and things that help them feel strong, and give them hope and courage. Then have participants write words, a message, or a poem about those people and things that have inspired them in their lives and showed them how strong they really are inside.

If you choose, you may want to pass out writing prompts to help participants focus their writing (see links in materials section). The word "strength" can be substituted with the words "hope," "courage," "inspiration," or "power."

When they have finished writing down their words of strength, hope, courage, and/or power, have each person transfer their words, messages or poems onto card stock or other heavy weight paper such as natural fiber paper.

When the writing is finished, use Tacky Glue to attach the paper onto their painted Mural Art Paper.


Step 5 (Final Step):
To create your scroll you will glue in place two dowels or chop sticks (depending on the size of your scroll) at the top and bottom of the scroll.
  
   Dowel, ribbon & beads at the top of the scroll
Fold over the top of the scroll to create a small (1") flap to insert the dowel into. Then have them put glue onto the back side of this fold, lay down the dowel, and fold the flap over to secure the dowel inside. Leave a small section of dowel (1" or less out from each side) to later hang ribbon from. Repeat at the bottom with a second dowel. To finish the scroll, tie the ribbon cord to each end of the dowel, adding beads onto the cord for added flair.

Closing Circle:
When everyone is finished, have each of the participants share their scrolls with each other. Give each participant a chance to share with the group and congratulate them on their beautiful creations and for sharing their strengths!

Encourage them to keep these scrolls as a special reminder of their strength and what inspires them. They can be hung on a wall, kept near a bed, or rolled up and carried with them.
Row.txt_description: This workshop combines writing and Liquid Watercolors beautifully. These fun watercolor materials can help us reach our feelings, and create an Inspirational Scroll.

Row.txt_code:
Objective:
This workshop allows survivors of abuse to use transform a suitcase as a means for expressing their journey, including their unique experience of survival. This art experience is meant to be a source of healing, with an emphasis on the creative process.

Materials:
Sandpaper
Glitter
Tissue paper
Buttons
Paintbrushes
Glue
Modge Podge
Fabric
Stickers
Cord or Yarn
Ribbon

Collage materials of all sorts
Stamps
Masking tape
StazOn inkpads
Decorative paper
Polyurethane varnish
Glue Dots (or other super adhesive glue)
Hardware (handles, luggage tags, etc)
Writing Paper and pens
Luggage and/or paper mache' boxes
Acrylic paint (pearlescent)		    

   






   
Time Frame:
Intro: 10 minutes
Opening: 10 minutes
Technical info: 5 minutes
Relaxation: 5 minutes
Creation: 70 minutes
Closing Circle: 15 minutes
Total Time: 1 hour and 10 minutes


Introduction:
Each life is a journey. We travel from place to place both physically and emotionally. On this journey there are things we want to take with us and things we want to leave behind. In this workshop, we will be taking suitcases, purses and travel objects and transforming them into visual statements that reflect who we are, where we have been and where we are going. The creative process will guide us as we transform suitcases using paint, collage, and decorative items to visually tell our stories.

Many of us are not comfortable openly talking about the profound affect sexual and domestic violence has had on our lives. My hope is for all of you to express yourselves in a different way, one that may feel safer for you. Art is a vehicle for us to express ourselves and feel safe. Everyone wants to be understood so as not to feel alone. We have our stories to share. Make this suitcase, which you have chosen, speak for you. There are no limits; there is no right or wrong way of telling your story.


Opening:
We are going to use a piece of cord as our timeline of remembering and letting go. We are going to acknowledge our feelings and honor where we have been and where we are going by knotting the cord. Take time to explore your feelings and memories as we travel through time (early childhood, childhood, adolescence, early adulthood, adulthood, and present time).

Technical Information:
Information pertaining to the art supplies is provided. Anything goes ... you can collage, paint, build on, whatever works for you. If you want a solid color background to work on you can paint a layer of any color of paint.

Relaxation:
During the relaxation, hold your cord in your hands and while you listen to the guided relaxation... you can think about your journey and tie knots as your memories encourage you to. During the relaxation it's good to sit with your feet flat on the floor, and the rest of your body relaxed! If it you feel comfortable, close your eyes and begin to picture in your mind... your journey... how old were you when it started...Begin to explore your feelings and memories through early childhood... what is your first memory...explore your memories from childhood through adolescence...what is your first memory of early adulthood...what memories come to mind when you first identified as an adult...remember to make a knot for each point in time...Now explore your feelings as an adult and in the present time...what recent memories do you have...When you feel you have knotted your cord to represent your time line, you can open your eyes and we'll begin to transform our suitcases.

Creation:
Transform your suitcase to reflect your story. Use the cord as part of your design. Take big risks! Be courageous, and remember it's your story; there isn't a right or wrong way to illustrate it. Don't be afraid to go WILD! Have fun!

Closing:
If participants end early, provide them with paper and pen and have them journal about their creative journey through their time line or suitcase.
Ask participants to share if they were able to express hard feelings, and how their creation has helped them to see where they are at in their journey now.
Row.txt_description: This workshop allows survivors of abuse to use transform a suitcase as a means for expressing their journey, including their unique experience of survival. This art experience is meant to be a source of healing, with an emphasis on the creative process.

Row.txt_code:
Objective:
The goal for this workshop is to empower survivors to think about places they want to go in their life...whether it is literal or figurative!
(This workshop is also great to do as a series with My Traveling Story workshop)


 Passport example
Materials:
Pre-made passport size journals or decorative paper for creating them
Collage materials of all sorts
Glue
Fabric
Stickers
Glitter
Ribbon
Stazon ink pads
Stamps
Decorative papers
Scissors
Binder or book stapler
    
    
Project set-up example
   
Ribbon
Hole Punch
Pens
Pencils
Markers
Cray Pas

Time Frame:
Intro: 10 minutes
Opening: 10 minutes
Technical info: 5 minutes
Relaxation: 10 minutes
Creation: 70 minutes
Closing Circle: 15 minutes
Total Time: 1 hour and 20 minutes

 
 Passport example
 
 
 
 
Introduction:
In real life passports are legal documents that are required to travel.  They give us permission to venture into other countries… places we haven’t been before! Today we are going to create our own passport… a passport to freedom.  A ‘legal’ document giving us permission to travel wherever we boldly dream to go! Today we will grant ourselves permission to travel to places we’ve never been before… these places can be literal or figurative!  Maybe we want to travel to a new job, a new neighborhood, a new loving relationship, a new adventure.  Where will you give yourself permission to fearlessly travel?  The possibilities are endless!  It is important to not censor yourself and allow all of the feelings and ideas this workshop yields to flow onto your artwork.  There is no right or wrong way to create your passport.  This is a chance to re-define who we are and what we consider possible.  In the past our voice, abilities and talent have been silenced by abusive partners.  Now is your time to speak out and discover where YOU want YOUR passport to take you. 

Opening:
Have the group members share places they would love to travel… whether literally or figuratively…  It can be a place they have always wanted to go, a new place, any place that is just for them.  It can also be any place you want to allow your mind, body, or spirit to travel.  Be creative and let the endless possibilities flow!   

Technical Information:
Explain the art supplies that are provided, make sure they understand they can use the pre-made passports or totally create their own.  Inform the participants they can use the hole punch and ribbon to create a passport book.  Encourage the participants to let you know if they need any additional supplies.  If possible give the group members a brief explanation of the project prior to the session and request they bring in any materials they might want to include.

Relaxation:
During the relaxation it's good to sit with your feet flat on the floor, your hands lying loosely in your lap and begin to feel your chair holding you very comfortably and safely! If it feels safe for you, close your eyes, breathe comfortably, and begin to picture in your mind... your passport…where do you want it to take you… where do you want to go… where have you always longed to travel (pause)… take a deep breath in and let it go… think about giving yourself permission to travel… breathe deeply and begin to feel your body intuitively relaxing… relax your toes, relax your feet, relax your ankles, feel the relaxation spreading to your calves... relax your calves... your knees... relax your legs… keep breathing deeply, letting out any stress your body might be holding, move your breath up to your thighs and feel them relaxing. Breath in deeply…let it go… and focus on your stomach… release any fear you might have about traveling to new places … feel the fear melting away, and courage taking its place!  Now move your awareness up to your shoulders and wiggle them around...relax your shoulders... feel your body intuitively relaxing more, and roll your head around allowing all the stress to leave your neck. Breathing deeply begin to relax your jaw, your mouth, your eyes, your head, wiggle your eyebrows and just feel totally relaxed. Taking another deep breath, allow your mind to just relax and think only about your passport and where you want it to take you...what you want to give yourself permission to do, to try, or to be?  Picture in your mind... your passport… where do you want it to take you… where do you want to go… where have you always longed to travel… take a deep breath and let it go… think about giving yourself permission to boldly do and go where ever you desire.  Now slowly  and gently begin to bring yourself back to the room, holding on to all the images you saw in your mind, slowly open your eyes and begin to create your passport to freedom!

Creation:
Begin to transform your passport into your ticket to anywhere! Take big risks! Be courageous, be bold… let your intuition take you where you want to go! Remember to let all judgment go... give yourself permission to create and let your inner yearnings out!  No one is here to judge or censor you...this is a safe place for you to respect your feelings and begin to define YOUR journey.  

 Passport example

Closing:
Give time for everyone to share what they experienced… where will they be traveling, how did it feel to give themselves permission to travel?  What new ideas, hopes, dreams or places did they discover?  Encourage each participant to share a page from their passport.
Row.txt_description: Through this workshop we will be creating a passport that grants us permission to travel wherever we want, whether our destination is literal or figurative!

Row.txt_code:
Objective:
Borrowing from the Huichol peoples of northwestern Mexico, this workshop gives the children an opportunity to create a symbol for safety.

 
Supplies for creating the God's Eye
 
Materials:
Craft sticks, Popsicle sticks or small twigs found in nature
Yarn - 3 or more colors
Embellishments (optional) - small bells, feathers, pom poms, buttons, beads, ribbons

Time Frame:
Approximately 1 hour

Age Range:
5 to 12 year old

Set Up:
For young children you might want to glue the two sticks together in advance, in the shape of a cross, and leave till firmly dry before wrapping the yarn.

Variation for age levels:
For younger children you can use a variegated yarn so they don't have to shift yarns to get more colors.
For older children can use smaller sticks (even toothpicks) or twigs and use a variety of novelty yarns, cord, ribbon, string and/or embroidery threads.

 
Creating God's Eye
 
Introduction:
Have the children sit in a circle. Show them a sample of a "God's Eye", and ask them if they have every seen one before. Explain to the children that this is a Mexican art form that has been around for a very long time. This craft continues to be part of Mexican tradition and culture and it is used as a good luck charm in the bedrooms of children and it's thought to protect them from harm. Let them know that that they are going to create God's Eye to help them feel safe.

Warm Up:
Take a ball of yarn and hanging on to a the tip of the yarn toss the ball to one of the children as they say their name and how they feel at that moment. Once they child has said her/his feeling ask her/him to hold on to a piece of the yarn then toss the ball to the next person ready to share their name and feeling. Keep doing it until all the children have shared and have the last child toss the ball back to you. You should end up with everyone connected by the string. Remind them that all of them and their feelings are welcome. Thank them for sharing.

Opening Circle:
Generate a brief discussion about safety. Ask they children if they know what it means to be safe. Explain that being safe is being free from harm or danger. Share with them that when we don't feel safe we usually feel afraid. Ask the children if they can think of a time that they felt afraid. If they have a hard time getting started, share something you are scared of. Let them know that right now your aren't afraid because you feel safe and protected. Reassure them that they are safe too and ask them to take a seat.

Creation:
 
Making the loop
 
 
Crossing the yarn over
 
 
Crossing the yarn under
 
 
Crossing the yarn over
 
 
Adding a second color
 
 
Laying the colors side by side
 
  
You will want to start with a brief demonstration of how to create a God's Eye. Ask the children to choose a color that represents safety to them to begin with. As they add new layers, ask them to choose a different color for each person they want to protect or keep safe.

Step One:
Loop about 6 inches of yarn and hold against the back of the top stick. Wrap the yarn around both the top stick and the loop. This will become your loop to hang the God's Eye when you are done creating it.

Step Two:
Cross two sticks at the center and tie them together with the end of a piece of yarn making an X shape. Do not cut the yarn. Wind the yarn several times, first from right to left diagonally, then left to right. Cover the center of the sticks.

Step Three:
Bring the yarn down and wrap it over, under and around the left "arm". Taking care to lay the yarn next to and not on top of the yarn already in place.

Step Four:
Wrap the yarn around the bottom "arm", then up and around the right"arm".

Step Five:
Wrap the yarn around the top stick and overlap the piece of yarn you have left dangling.

Step Six:
When you are ready you can tie a different color yarn onto the old one with a tight knot.

Step Seven:
Continue wrapping in this way, left, bottom, right, top, until almost all the stick is covered.
Tie off at the end and tuck under.

As an optional finishing touch, tie several strands of yarn or ribbon to the bottom stick and add beads, feathers or any other decoration you like. You might need a dot of glue to secure the tassel.

Closing Circle:
Have the children hold up the God's Eye they created and talk about how why they chose the colors they chose, who they want to keep safe and why. Then ask them how they will use their God's Eye.
Row.txt_description: Borrowing from the Huichol peoples of northwestern Mexico,this workshop gives the children an opportunity to create a God's Eye as a symbol of safety.
Row.txt_tips:
You can make several God's Eyes in a variety of sizes and create a mobile.

A God's Eye can be hung almost anywhere, you can also make them as ornaments for a holiday tree.

Row.txt_code:
Hands Mandala from Wausau, Wisconsin
Objective:
To place your hands into a circle of support of all who are helping build a violence-free future by creating a healing hands mandala.  To bring powerful voices, images, and broad participation to Domestic Violence Awareness Month events through art letting children and adults surviving domestic violence know their voices, hands and hearts do not stand alone.

  


 
Women working on their Hands Mandalas.
  
Materials:
Black paper - 20” by 20” squares
White colored pencils
Pencil sharpeners

Timeframe:
Total time: 2 hours—allow more time if needed.   
  


 
"Trying to break free into the Light."
  

Introduction:
Everyone has the power within themselves to help heal emotional and physical pain.  Today we will discover the beauty we can create by allowing the light to radiate through our hands onto this black paper.

Technical Info:
Demonstrate on a scrap of black paper how to use the white pencil to make gradations of light.  Start out by pressing very hard on the pencil until the black is totally covered, then gradually lighten the pressure until you see black again. 

Creation:
Have them practice with you until they feel comfortable.  Explain that you can draw as many hands as you want, in different positions, crossing over each other, etc.  Encourage each person to just do what feels comfortable.  When they have completed placement of the hands, they can work on the luminous part by using the white pencil.  Some may want to use other colors besides white, which is fine.  But encourage lighter ones such as yellow or light orange.  Have everyone walk around the table to see what others have done.
  


 
"Reaching for Peace with the Worlds.  My art describes peace and harmony.  May God bless us all, so let us continue to reach for the sky and stars."
  


Closing:
Ask each person to explain what their Mandala means to them.  Were they able to feel a different kind of energy coming through their hands?  If they are not finished, encourage them to take them home.  (They will need a white pencil to take along.)  

We found that clients came back asking for more paper to work on more Mandalas.  They found them very peaceful and relaxing.

Exhibit:
In Wausau, Wisconsin, we displayed over 35 different mandalas during the month of October.  We used this occasion as our Open House.  We draped black, red, and violet fabric over the walls in the hallway and hung the Mandalas from the fabric.  
It was very beautiful.  

Many participants also added words, which were typed and hung on the bottom of each Mandala.  We cut them out in circles: then pasted them to white poster board.  

I hope you enjoy this workshop!




Details from some of the mandalas.
  

Quick Alternative:
If you'd prefer a faster alternative, simply use the white tempera paint to place your hand prints onto the page and add any words or designs in pencil around your hands.  Feel free to encourage family members, young and old to join in!

For clear hand prints, practice on scratch paper.  Try rubbing the paint between your flat hands like lotion to distribute evenly.  Then press firmly onto the paper.  See what happens as you make a new print without adding more paint.  Do you like the lighter version? 

 
"I'm trying to teach my son how to be gentle."
Row.txt_description: Project welcoming community to support Zazou event.
